title: What's the future of the internet?
summary: Josh and Chuck speculate on the future of the Internet, opening with current usage statistics from Pew Research (internet adoption growth from 2001 to today, and what adults do online). They then discuss download speeds and record data transfer rates (Bell Labs laser transfer, fiber optic records), predicting faster wireless and landline access. The hosts cover net neutrality, the December 2010 FCC ruling and its wireless exception, and the risk of a tiered, corporatized Internet. They discuss tethered appliances and walled gardens (Apple's App Store, Xbox Live), the Flash vs. HTML5 dispute, and a book by Jonathan Zittrain. Nicholas Carr's "Is Google Making Us Stupid" and concerns about smartphones and memory are discussed. They close with predictions from Mashable's six web pioneers (Very Glick, Jeremy Stoppelman, Ryan Ozimek, and a Drupal founder) and then answer listener Facebook questions on unrelated topics.
topics: Nicholas Carr Is Google Making Us Stupid

entities.name: The Future of the Internet and How to Stop It

segments.title: Opening and episode framing
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the topic of the future of the Internet, note that few people make concrete predictions, and mention coworker John Strickland's work on the subject.

segments.title: Internet adoption and usage statistics
segments.summary: Pew Research figures are cited: US adult internet adoption rose from about 14 percent in 2001 to 60 percent by November 2001 comparison and about 77 percent now, with breakdowns by gender and household income. They also list common daily online activities such as email, search, news, social networking, weather, and video.

segments.title: Download speeds and data transfer records
segments.summary: The hosts define effective data transfer rate and discuss the gap between advertised speeds and actual speeds. They cite a Bell Labs laser record of 100 petabytes per second and a fiber optic record of about 26 terabytes per second, and predict faster wireless and landline access.

segments.title: Net neutrality and the FCC ruling
segments.summary: Net neutrality is explained as keeping the Internet open regardless of provider. The hosts describe the risk of ISPs favoring certain sites, the December 2010 FCC ruling that left a wireless exception, and concerns about a divided, corporatized Internet. They argue for a Darwinian, level playing field.

segments.title: Walled gardens, tethered appliances, and Flash
segments.summary: The hosts discuss device makers creating walled gardens such as Apple's iPhone App Store and Xbox Live, which limit access to certain parts of the Internet. They also discuss Apple's refusal to support Adobe Flash and the rise of HTML5, and Jonathan Zittrain's book on the future of the Internet.

segments.title: Smartphones, memory, and Nicholas Carr
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Nicholas Carr's article 'Is Google Making Us Stupid' and how skimming online information may change how people think and remember. They share personal concerns about attention and memory and the loss of tip-of-the-tongue moments, and mention smartphone etiquette.

segments.title: Web pioneers' predictions
segments.summary: The hosts review predictions from Mashable's six web pioneers: Very Glick on invisible ubiquitous access, Jeremy Stoppelman on augmented reality, Ryan Ozimek on cloud focus, and a Drupal founder on more websites and devices.

segments.title: Listener questions and off-topic chat
segments.summary: The hosts answer Facebook questions on unrelated topics such as favorite music, drinks, Academy Awards, and Looney Tunes versus Disney ducks, and invite listener predictions by email.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck invite listeners to send predictions and questions, and promote the Stuff from the Future video podcast.
